title: Dichotomy for consistent query answering under primary keys
area: Database theory and finite model theory
formal:
For every fixed finite relational schema with one designated nonempty primary key for each relation, and every fixed Boolean conjunctive query \(q\) over that schema, is the language \(\operatorname{CERTAINTY}(q)\) either in deterministic polynomial time or coNP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions?

The input to this language is an explicitly represented finite database \(D\), possibly violating its keys. It is accepted exactly when \(q\) is true in every inclusion-maximal subdatabase of \(D\) that satisfies the keys. Repeated occurrences of a relation in \(q\), called self-joins, are allowed.
definitions:
A schema lists relation names and their positive integer arities. Each relation has a fixed nonempty subset of its positions as its primary key. A database is a finite set of tuples for each relation, with values encoded as finite binary strings. A key is satisfied if any two tuples agreeing in all key positions also agree in every position. A subdatabase deletes tuples without inserting or changing values. A repair is such a subdatabase that satisfies all keys and cannot be enlarged by putting back any deleted tuple while still satisfying them. Thus, for each nonempty group of conflicting tuples with one key value, a repair chooses exactly one tuple; this is inclusion maximality, not an optimization over all possible edits.

A Boolean conjunctive query is a finite nonempty conjunction of relational atoms with all its variables existentially quantified; variables may repeat within and across atoms, and fixed constants are allowed. It contains no negation, disjunction, inequality, function symbol or aggregation. Truth means that some assignment of its variables makes every atom a stored tuple. Query and schema, including keys, are fixed separately for each language; only the database varies. Time is measured in the total bit length of its explicit encoding, with constants and polynomial degree allowed to depend on the fixed query/schema.

P denotes languages decided by deterministic polynomial-time Turing machines. A language is in coNP if its complement has polynomial-size certificates verifiable in deterministic polynomial time. It is coNP-complete if it is in coNP and every coNP language reduces to it by one polynomial-time computable map preserving yes/no answers. The question asserts that every fixed query has one of these two complexities. It does not additionally require a computable classifier taking a query as input, nor assume that P differs from coNP.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated proposition. Results for a restricted query family do not settle its universal scope. A conditional negative result must retain its unproved assumptions and is not an unconditional refutation.
why: Conflicting primary-key records are routine in integrated data. This question asks whether every fixed database query is either efficiently answerable with certainty across all repairs or computationally complete for a standard hard class.

context_blocks.text: Consistent answers retain only conclusions that survive every repair of inconsistent records. The difficulty comes from universal quantification over these alternative databases, even though evaluating the fixed query on one consistent database is easy.

The ICDT 2023 paper formulates the unrestricted primary-key dichotomy and gives a common polynomial-time method covering the known self-join-free and path-query tractable cases. It also explains why that method does not capture all tractable queries with self-joins.
For queries without repeated relation names, the 2019 result sharpens the tractable side to logarithmic space. That restricted classification leaves the universal self-join target stated here.
